title: Managing multiple Tally accounts
text: Store account’s key environment variable .Renviron (e.g. via usethis::edit_r_environ()): TALLY_API_KEY default account, TALLY_API_KEY_<NAME> named accounts. <NAME> part becomes account name use R, ’s case-insensitive: Restart R editing .Renviron, check tallyr can see tally_accounts(): default account comes first TALLY_API_KEY set, followed named accounts alphabetical order. don’t need default account : prefer, give every account name skip bare TALLY_API_KEY.
code: TALLY_API_KEY=tly-xxxx TALLY_API_KEY_WORK=tly-yyyy TALLY_API_KEY_RLADIES=tly-zzzz tally_accounts() #> [1] "default" "rladies" "work"

title: Managing multiple Tally accounts
text: tally_use_account() switches active account rest session. Every tallyr function uses account: Switch back default account NULL "default": tally_use_account() invisibly returns name account active switch, can restore afterwards – handy scripts functions shouldn’t disturb session’s state: ask account key set, tally_use_account() errors immediately, telling environment variable expected accounts available – won’t find three calls later confusing authentication failure.
code: tally_use_account("work") #> ✔ Using Tally account "work"  tally_forms() # uses the "work" account tally_whoami() # reports the "work" user tally_use_account("default") #> ✔ Using the default Tally account previous <- tally_use_account("rladies") #> ✔ Using Tally account "rladies"  # ... work with the "rladies" account ...  tally_use_account(previous) #> ✔ Using the default Tally account

title: Managing multiple Tally accounts
text: don’t switch accounts make single call someone else. Every tallyr function touches API takes account argument: account argument affects call; session’s active account unchanged.
code: tally_forms(account = "rladies") tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", account = "work") tally_whoami(account = "work")

title: Managing multiple Tally accounts
text: tallyr function needs API key, decides account use order: explicit account argument, supplied one. session’s active account, ’ve switched tally_use_account(). Otherwise, default account. default account, key looked first tallyr.api_key R option, TALLY_API_KEY environment variable. option exists can set key single session options(tallyr.api_key = "tly-..."), without touching .Renviron. named account’s key comes TALLY_API_KEY_<NAME> environment variable; tallyr.api_key option never consulted named accounts.

title: Managing multiple Tally accounts
text: tally_whoami() tally_sitrep() take account argument, can confirm Tally user key belongs without switching: key isn’t behaving expected, tally_sitrep() reports active key found, whether looks like Tally key, whether authenticates – see vignette("troubleshooting").
code: tally_whoami(account = "work") #> ✔ Authenticated with Tally as Ada Lovelace (ada@lovelace.industries)  tally_sitrep(account = "work")

title: Working with submission data
text: one row per submission. first three columns always: submission_id: Tally’s identifier submission. submitted_at: submitted, POSIXct date-time UTC. is_completed: whether respondent finished form, abandoned partway (“partial” submission). remaining columns form’s questions, form order, one column per question.

what: Column names come from question titles
title: Working with submission data
text: question column named question’s title, exactly appears form – including spaces punctuation. keeps columns self-describing, cost names need backticks R code: form two questions title, names made unique appending ... column’s position, way tibble::as_tibble() repairs duplicate names:
code: feedback$`What's your name?` names(tally_submissions("9aKp3T")) #> [1] "submission_id"        "submitted_at"         "is_completed" #> [4] "What's your name?"    "Favourite colour?...5" "Favourite colour?...6"

title: Working with submission data
text: Every question column character vector, whatever question type. tallyr uses formatted answer Tally API provides consistent string representation across question types, falling back raw answer (multiple parts joined ", ") formatted version. practice means: Text questions give text entered. Multiple-choice checkbox questions give chosen option labels, comma-separated one selected (e.g. "Teal, Purple"). Numeric date questions arrive strings, convert want compute (see ). question respondent didn’t answer NA. Partial submissions typically NA every question point respondent stopped.

title: Working with submission data
text: examples use dplyr friends, nothing tibble requires – base R works just well.

title: Working with submission data
text: Question titles make awkward variable names, renaming usually first step:
code: library(dplyr)  feedback <- tally_submissions("3xLJ5V") |>   rename(     name = `What's your name?`,     sessions = `Which sessions did you attend?`,     comments = `Any other comments?`   )

title: Working with submission data
text: Since answers arrive strings, convert columns really numbers, dates, factors:
code: ratings <- tally_submissions("5cRw8Y") |>   rename(rating = `How would you rate the event? (1-5)`) |>   mutate(rating = as.integer(rating))  ratings |>   count(rating)

title: Working with submission data
text: Checkbox answers several selections come back one comma-separated string. analyse individual options, split rows:
code: library(tidyr)  feedback |>   separate_longer_delim(sessions, delim = ", ") |>   count(sessions, sort = TRUE)

title: Working with submission data
text: submitted_at POSIXct UTC. report local time zone, convert lubridate::with_tz() (format() base R):
code: feedback |>   mutate(submitted_local = lubridate::with_tz(submitted_at, "Europe/London"))

title: Working with submission data
text: filtering better done API import, since reduces ’s downloaded. tally_submissions() can restrict completion status date: Anything finer-grained – filtering answers, say – job dplyr::filter() import: overview rest package, see vignette("tallyr").
code: # only submissions where the respondent finished the form tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", filter = "completed")  # only abandoned, partial submissions tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", filter = "partial")  # a date window; accepts Dates, date-times, or ISO 8601 strings tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", start_date = "2026-01-01", end_date = "2026-06-30") feedback |>   filter(!is.na(comments))

title: Get started with tallyr
text: Tally uses personal API keys. Create one Tally Settings > API keys, store TALLY_API_KEY environment variable .Renviron, e.g. via usethis::edit_r_environ(): Restart R editing .Renviron new variable picked . confirm ’re authenticated, run tally_whoami(): something isn’t working, tally_sitrep() gives full situation report setup, recommendations fixing anything ’s wrong – see vignette("troubleshooting"). one Tally account, can store key switch – see vignette("multiple-accounts").
code: TALLY_API_KEY=tly-xxxx tally_whoami() #> ✔ Authenticated with Tally as Ada Lovelace (ada@example.com)

title: Get started with tallyr
text: tally_forms() returns tibble forms access , one row per form: Alongside form’s name status ("BLANK", "DRAFT", "PUBLISHED" "DELETED"), tibble includes id ’ll need import submissions. ID appears form’s URL tally., can also read directly. restrict results particular workspaces, pass IDs:
code: tally_forms() #> # A tibble: 2 × 8 #>   id     name                status    number_of_submissions is_closed #>   <chr>  <chr>               <chr>                     <int> <lgl> #> 1 3xLJ5V Conference feedback PUBLISHED                    42 FALSE #> 2 7bQm2W Workshop signup     DRAFT                         0 FALSE #> # ℹ 3 more variables: workspace_id <chr>, created_at <dttm>, #> #   updated_at <dttm> tally_forms(workspace_ids = "w4ZZ9R")

title: Get started with tallyr
text: tally_submissions() imports form’s submissions wide tibble: one row per submission, one column per question, question titles column names: first three columns always submission_id, submitted_at is_completed; rest form’s questions, form order. details answers represented tidy , see vignette("submission-data").
code: feedback <- tally_submissions("3xLJ5V") feedback #> # A tibble: 42 × 5 #>   submission_id submitted_at        is_completed `What's your name?` #>   <chr>         <dttm>              <lgl>        <chr> #> 1 nWxyzA        2026-06-01 10:00:00 TRUE         Ada #> 2 nWxyzB        2026-06-02 11:30:00 TRUE         Grace #> # ℹ 40 more rows #> # ℹ 1 more variable: `How was the conference?` <chr>

title: Get started with tallyr
text: default get submissions, including partial ones (respondent started didn’t submit form). Use filter restrict one : can also restrict date start_date end_date, accept Date, date-time, ISO 8601 string:
code: tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", filter = "completed") tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", filter = "partial") tally_submissions("3xLJ5V", start_date = "2026-01-01") tally_submissions(   "3xLJ5V",   filter = "completed",   start_date = "2026-01-01",   end_date = "2026-06-30" )

title: Get started with tallyr
text: Tally API returns results pages, limits clients 100 requests per minute. don’t need manage either: tally_forms() tally_submissions() fetch pages automatically, every request throttled stay within rate limit.

title: Troubleshooting your Tally setup
text: tally_sitrep() checks everything relevant tallyr working: accounts keys available active, whether active account’s key found (), whether looks like Tally key, whether ’re online, whether key actually authenticates. ends recommendations fixing anything ’s wrong, never errors, whatever state setup . healthy setup looks like : sections walk situations can catch.

No account keys found in environment variables #> ℹ Active account: "default" (the default) #> #> ── API key #> ✖ No API key found for account "default" #> #> ── Connectivity #> ✔ Internet: online #> ℹ Skipping API connection test #> #> ── Recommendations #> • Create an API key at <https://tally.so/settings/api-keys> #> • Set `TALLY_API_KEY` in your '.Renviron' (e.g. with #> `usethis::edit_r_environ()`) #> ── Recommendations #> • Create an API key at <https://tally.so/settings/api-keys> #> • Set `TALLY_API_KEY` in your '.Renviron' (e.g. with #> `usethis::edit_r_environ()`) #> • Or switch to an account with a key: `tally_use_account("work")`

title: Troubleshooting your Tally setup
